en: So we have this project here, this image
optimization project which we worked on.
Now, thus far, I always
used this tool
by running this optimize images script, or
we could run this command here, of course,
directly in the command line. And there is
nothing wrong with this, but Bun has another
nice feature which can be very useful if you
wanted to
distribute a tool like this to other people.
Because right now, if I wanted to share this
tool with someone else,
that someone else needs to install Bun on
their system, right? Because we're using the
Bun runtime, we're using the Bun tool here.
So Bun must be installed on the machine
where you wanna run this program.
And if I wanna share that with a friend who
doesn't even know about Bun, that of course
could be a bit annoying.
And that's where another nice feature of Bun
comes into play. The single file executable
feature.
Bun allows you
to compile
any TypeScript or JavaScript code into a
standalone executable, into a single file
that can be shared with others, that can be
executed on any system, Windows, Linux,
macOS,
without Bun needing to be installed.
And it's this command which we can execute
to produce such a single file executable.
Obviously, we must plug in our file name
here. So the root entry point of our
program, in my case, optimize-images.ts,
and then --compile compiles that to a single
file executable.
So here I'll name this opt-image.
That will be the name of the
executable of the tool that will be created.
And if I run this,
it'll go ahead and now I have this opt-image
thing here.
And that's now a binary file that can be
executed like this.
On Windows, it should have had.exe
extension already.
And that then is this entire tool bundled
into one executable. And that's of course a
super useful feature for distributing code.
Now, it's worth noting that you can also set
specific targets. By default, it'll use your
operating system as a target. So in my case,
macOS.
If I knew that I wanted to build for
Windows, I could add --target and then for
Windows x64,
bun-windows-x64, for example.
Or if you know that you're only targeting
recent versions of Windows, you could use
the modern version.
So I'll set my target to bun-windows-x64.
That'll go ahead and do its thing.
And now I got that
.exe file here, which I could share with
Windows users. And you can do the same thing
for other operating systems too, of course.
And that therefore is of course an extremely
valuable feature when building utility
tools, CLI tools like the one we have here,
because that makes sharing them so much
easier.
